$meta.description: Text is stored in strings of Unicode characters. Write strings by surrounding them with quotes. If you need to include a quotation mark in the string, write it twice.
example: print(a + b) // concatinate a and b

remove.description: Returns a new `string` with the provided value removed. Any value other than `null` can be passed, but note that it will be cast to a string. If `null` is passed, this method will throw an error, preventing further script execution.
example: myString = "42 as an answer is wrong"

hasIndex.description: Returns one when the numeric index exists in the `string`, otherwise zero. A non-number index also returns zero.
example: myString = "42 as an answer is wrong"
print("String does not contain index of 1.")

insert.description: Returns a `string` with the newly inserted `string` at the provided index. If the passed index is not a `number`, this method throws an error, preventing further script execution.
example: myString = "42 as an answer is wrong"

indexOf.description: Returns a `number` which indicates the first matching index of the provided value inside the `list`. Optionally a start index can be provided. In case the value does not exist inside the `string` a `null` gets returned.
example: myString = "42 as an answer is wrong"

lastIndexOf.description: Returns a `number` which indicates the last matching index of the provided value inside the `list`. In case the value does not exist inside the `string` a `-1` gets returned. If the provided searchStr is not a `string`, this method will return `null`.
example: myString = "42 as an answer is wrong"

split.description: Splits a `string` with a regular expression and returns a `list` of strings. An empty separator returns one character per list item. Invalid regex options return `"split: Invalid regex option"`; an invalid .NET regex pattern returns its error message as a `string`. Invalid argument types return `null`; regex timeouts still raise a runtime error.
example: myString = "42 as an answer is wrong"

replace.description: Returns a `string` with regular-expression matches replaced. Invalid regex options return `"replace: Invalid regex option"`; an invalid .NET regex pattern returns its error message as a `string`. Empty patterns, invalid argument types, and regex timeouts still raise runtime errors.
example: myString = "42 as an answer is wrong"

trim.description: Returns a new `string` stripped of any spacing at the beginning and ending.

indexes.description: Returns a `list` where each item is a `number` representing all available indexes in the `string`.

code.description: Returns a `number` representing the Unicode code of the first character of the `string`.

len.description: Returns a `number` representing the length of the `string`.

lower.description: Returns a new `string` in which all characters are transformed into lowercase.

upper.description: Returns a new `string` in which all characters are transformed into uppercase.

val.description: Returns a `number` which is parsed from the `string`. In case the `string` is not numeric it will return a zero.

values.description: Returns a `list` where each item is a `string` representing all available characters in the `string`. Could be compared to using `split` but without any separator.

to_int.description: Parses a `string` as an invariant-culture double and returns the resulting `number`, accepting forms such as `"1.5"`, `" 1e3 "`, `"1,000"`, and `"(5)"`. Non-numeric text is returned unchanged, a `number` is returned as-is, and other types return `null`. The global function defaults `self` to zero.

is_match.description: Uses regular expression to check if a string matches a certain pattern. If it matches, it will return a `number` with the value one. If it does not match, the value of the `number` will be zero. If any provided arguments deviate from the method signature types, if the pattern is empty, if the provided [regexOptions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/base-types/regular-expression-options) are invalid, or if the regular expression times out, an error will be thrown, preventing further script execution.
example: myString = "42 as an answer is wrong"

matches.description: Returns a `map` whose numeric keys are match positions and whose values are the matching strings. Invalid regex options return `"matches: Invalid regex option"`; an invalid .NET regex pattern returns its error message as a `string`. Empty patterns, invalid argument types, and regex timeouts still raise runtime errors. `is_match` continues to raise for invalid regex options.
example: myString = "42 as an answer is wrong"
